content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To clean chicken livers, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Rinse the livers under cold running water (2 minutes)
Step 2. Set up a clean cutting board and sharp paring knife (3 minutes)
Step 3. Prepare a bowl of ice water for soaking (2 minutes)
Step 4. Pat the trimmed livers dry with paper towels (2 minutes)
Step 5. Remove the livers from the grocery packaging (1 minute)
Step 6. Place the cleaned livers into the ice water bath (1 minute)
Step 7. Separate the two main lobes of each liver (4 minutes)
Step 8. Clear a workspace on the kitchen counter (5 minutes)
Step 9. Sanitize the sink after the initial rinse (10 minutes)
Step 10. Locate the colander in the cupboard (1 minute)
Step 11. Wash hands thoroughly with antibacterial soap (40 seconds)
Step 12. Sharpen the paring knife (5 minutes)
Step 13. Put on a protective kitchen apron (1 minute)
Step 14. Inspect the livers for any greenish bile staining (3 minutes)
Step 15. Organize the workspace into "dirty" and "clean" zones (2 minutes)
Step 16. Dispose of any connective tissue into the trash (2 minutes)
Step 17. Gather small containers for the trimmed bits (2 minutes)
Step 18. Set out a waste bowl for scraps (1 minute)
Step 19. Wipe down the knife handle to maintain grip (30 seconds)
Step 20. Put on a pair of disposable food-prep gloves (1 minute)
Step 21. Add a pinch of salt to the soaking bowl (30 seconds)
Step 22. Trim away the tough white connective tissue (8 minutes)
Step 23. Drain the excess liquid from the rinsing bowl (1 minute)
Step 24. Prepare a secondary container for the finished livers (2 minutes)
Step 25. Check the livers for any remaining blood clots (4 minutes)
Step 26. Carefully cut out any visible veins (6 minutes)
Step 27. Lay the livers flat on the board for better visibility (2 minutes)
Step 28. Rinse the cutting board to remove surface blood (2 minutes)
Step 29. Submerge the livers fully in the cold water (1 minute)
Step 30. Position the waste bowl within easy reach (30 seconds)
Step 31. Retrieve a fresh roll of paper towels (1 minute)
Step 32. Clear any unnecessary items from the backsplash (4 minutes)
Step 33. Set the knife down safely between cuts (10 seconds)
Step 34. Wipe the blade of the knife clean (30 seconds)
Step 35. Lay out a clean kitchen towel (1 minute)
Step 36. Spray the counter with disinfectant (3 minutes)
Step 37. Sort the livers by size for even cooking later (5 minutes)
Step 38. Place the livers in a final storage container (2 minutes)
Step 39. Cut away the fatty deposits near the center (5 minutes)
Step 40. Retrieve a small bowl for the discarded bile ducts (1 minute)
Step 41. Label the storage container with the date (1 minute)
Step 42. Scrub the cutting board with hot soapy water (5 minutes)
Step 43. Check for any missed stringy bits (3 minutes)
Step 44. Slice the livers into uniform bite-sized pieces (6 minutes)
Step 45. Transfer the livers to a marinating dish (1 minute)
Step 46. Season the livers lightly with pepper (30 seconds)
Step 47. Remove any small fragments of fat (4 minutes)
Step 48. Check the kitchen lighting for better visibility (1 minute)
Step 49. Double-check the lobes for internal clots (3 minutes)
Step 50. Toss the used paper towels into the bin (30 seconds)
Step 51. Cover the container with plastic wrap (1 minute)
Step 52. Sterilize the workstation area (7 minutes)
Step 53. Gather all necessary cleaning tools and bowls (5 minutes)
Step 54. Inspect the paring knife for nicks (1 minute)
Step 55. Final visual inspection of the batch (2 minutes)
Step 56. Tie the trash bag containing the scraps (1 minute)
Step 57. Carefully excise any bile-stained yellow spots (4 minutes)
Step 58. Put on a clean face mask for hygiene (1 minute)
Step 59. Clean the tips of the kitchen shears (2 minutes)
Step 60. Refrigerate the cleaned livers immediately (1 minute)
